title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.

definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.

providers.name: Databricks (AWS baseline)
providers.scope_notes: AWS IP-access-list docs require Enterprise tier. Azure/GCP capabilities and licensing must be checked separately.

controls.name: IP access lists
controls.what: Restrict account console/account APIs and workspace/workspace APIs to approved IPs.
controls.setting: Account console IP access lists; workspace IP Access List API
controls.quote: The default allows connections from any IP address.

controls.name: Context-based ingress policies
controls.what: Account-level allow/deny rules combining identity, network source and request scope, e.g. pinning service principals to trusted networks.
controls.quote: allow and deny rules that combine who is calling, from where they are calling, and what they can reach

controls.name: App connections (disable published or custom OAuth apps)
controls.what: Removing an app connection disables it and breaks existing connections.
controls.setting: Account console > Settings > App connections > Remove; published-app-integration / custom-app-integration CLI
controls.quote: Disabling an application breaks the application connection, so use caution when disabling OAuth applications.

controls.name: App connection token TTLs
controls.what: Sets access token (default 60 min) and refresh token (default 10080 min) lifetimes for custom apps.
controls.setting: Account console > Settings > App connections > edit app
controls.quote: The refresh token time-to-live (TTL) in minutes. Default: `10080`.

controls.name: Single-use refresh tokens
controls.what: Makes refresh tokens single-use for an app integration; API only.
controls.quote: You can only configure additional OAuth security features (such as single-use refresh tokens) through the API.

controls_unknown: No account-wide switch to disable PATs across all workspaces was found; the toggle is per workspace.
Whether IP access lists explicitly cover PAT/OAuth API calls is implied (workspace-level APIs) but not stated.
Whether context-based ingress rules can distinguish auth method (PAT vs OAuth) is not stated.
How to update or delete federation policies, and how to revoke an individual OAuth secret, were not covered on the fetched pages.
TTL min/max ranges, and whether built-in databricks-cli app follows app-connection TTL defaults, not confirmed.
Single-use refresh token details page returned 404; defaults per app not confirmed.
Azure/GCP capabilities and tiers not checked.

authentication.summary: A user signs in through the browser and consents; the CLI, SDK or app then receives a Databricks OAuth access token (and refresh token) and sends it as a bearer token. Works at account level or for one workspace; the CLI caches tokens in ~/.databricks/token-cache.json.

federation.details: The user signs in interactively (which can go through the account's SSO); no external token is exchanged on this path. Token exchange of external IdP tokens is the separate external token federation path.

ip_restriction.boundary: Account and workspace IP access lists cover the UI and REST APIs at each level and require the Enterprise tier. Private IPs from PrivateLink traffic are not filtered by them.

lifetime.summary: Default 1 h; app integrations accept 5 min–24 h

renewal.summary: Refresh tokens get new access tokens; app-connection default refresh TTL is 10080 min (7 days), configurable 5 min–90 days. With single-use refresh tokens (rotation) each new refresh token gets a fresh TTL, optionally capped by an absolute session lifetime (Beta).

administration.summary: Account admins manage OAuth app connections (custom and published apps), their token TTLs and single-use refresh tokens; disabling an app breaks its connections. Revoking user consent does not invalidate existing refresh tokens. Workspace permissions/ACLs govern what the user can do.
administration.conditions: TTL defaults and ranges are documented for app connections generally; whether the built-in databricks-cli app uses the same defaults was not confirmed. Single-use refresh tokens are on by default only for some partner apps.

sso.details: Issuance needs a browser sign-in, which uses SSO when account SSO is on; existing refresh tokens keep working.

offboard.details: Tokens of a deactivated user cannot authenticate; SCIM removal deactivates the user.

inventory.details: Users can view their own consent per app (/api/2.0/oauth-app-integrations/<id>/user-consent/me); no admin-wide token list found.

sso.ui: Account console > Security > Identity provider setup > Authentication > single sign-on

reads.api: SQL: SELECT * FROM system.access.audit WHERE service_name='workspace' AND action_name='workspaceExport' (filter user_identity.email)

offboard.ui: Remove the user from the IdP account-level SCIM connector (deactivates the user)

token_format.notes: Access/refresh token format not documented. GitHub types: databricks_oauth_refresh_token, databricks_oauth_single_use_refresh_token_parent/child, databricks_oauth_code, databricks_workspace_session_token. CLI caches in ~/.databricks/token-cache.json.

log_sources.name: Databricks audit logs (system.access.audit system table / audit log delivery)
log_sources.notes: Account- and workspace-level events; account-level rows have workspace_id 0. No general retention stated on the table page; events of a deleted workspace older than 14 days are removed.

log_sources.name: Endpoint file ~/.databricks/token-cache.json
log_sources.notes: Cached access/refresh tokens on the user's machine; theft target.

credential_id_fields.notes: For an OAuth app, the app name

lifecycle_events.notes: Token minted; grant_type, scope, expires_in, client_id
API call authorized via OAuth token

anomaly_cues: mintOAuthToken (refresh) for a user from an IP never seen in that user's oidcBrowserLogin events (stolen token-cache.json)
refresh grants continuing long after the user's last interactive login
updateCustomAppIntegration changing redirect_url to an unknown host
new custom app integration with long refresh_token_ttl_in_minutes
user_agent mismatch between login and later API calls

containment.steps: Deactivate the user (account level); delete or disable the OAuth app integration; shorten refresh_token_ttl_in_minutes / enable single-use refresh tokens and absolute_session_lifetime_in_minutes; delete local token-cache.json.
containment.notes: Revoking consent doesn't invalidate existing tokens; refresh tokens work until expiry. No documented per-token revoke for OAuth tokens. Access tokens last one hour.

sample_query.query: SELECT user_identity.email, request_params['client_id'] AS client_id, request_params['grant_type'] AS grant_type, source_ip_address, user_agent, count(*) AS n FROM system.access.audit WHERE service_name = 'accounts' AND action_name IN ('mintOAuthToken','oidcBrowserLogin') AND event_date >= current_date() - INTERVAL 14 DAYS GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY user_identity.email
sample_query.purpose: Compare token-mint IPs to browser-login IPs per user
